messages:
Morgan (Finance): Hey team - BrightPath's Aug invoice (INV-2026-057) just landed with ~2.4x burst charges vs their reserved commit. Customer is asking for a breakdown and potential SLA credit. Can SRE/ops confirm whether this was genuine burst traffic or a metering issue?

Jess (SRE): Looking. Preliminary: we show a spike on 2026-08-18 03:00 UTC that pushed them into burst for ~2.5h. Likely real traffic. Giving query now.

Jess (SRE): ```sql
SELECT ts, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, commit_id
FROM usage_events
WHERE customer_id='brightpath' AND ts BETWEEN '2026-08-18T02:30:00Z' AND '2026-08-18T06:00:00Z'
ORDER BY ts;
```

Naomi (Acct): Can you also confirm which Dedicated pool they were on and whether any fallback(s) to hosted occurred? Customer claims they never hit hosted endpoints.

Jess (SRE): They were on dp-reserved-42 in us-west-2. No automated fallback logs to hosted in that window. I see heavier KV-cache misses due to many short-lived chat sessions which increased per-token cost.

Bryan (Ops): Noted. There was a mesh-restart on dp-reserved-42 a day earlier (2026-08-17) for kernel update, but all nodes were back and healthy before the 18th spike. No config changes during the spike.

Sam (Sales): Customer says their app had a bad client loop and they're apologizing. They're asking if we can waive the burst charge this time — they have an active renewal discussion. What do we recommend?

Morgan (Finance): If it's an application-level runaway, standard policy is chargeable. But for retention we can consider a negotiated one-off credit capped at 25% of the burst invoice if sales signs renewal. Need approval from VP Finance.

Naomi (Acct): BillingBot, can you attach the invoice lines and token-level breakdown for INV-2026-057?

BillingBot: Attached: invoice_INV-2026-057.pdf, line_items.csv, token_breakdown_2026-08-01_31.csv (uploaded).

Morgan (Finance): Uploaded files look consistent with SRE's numbers. Burst tokens = 18,450,300; reserved included tokens = 7,500,000; overage = 10,950,300 -> $8,215.

Naomi (Acct): Customer requests SLA credit if any platform-side loss contributed. SRE confirmed no fallback and no regressions. Seems customer app caused it.

Sam (Sales): I'll propose a goodwill credit of $2,000 contingent on accelerated renewal (signed by end of Q3). Does Finance approve?

Morgan (Finance): Please escalate to Elisa (VP Finance) for one-off approval. If Elisa signs off, Naomi will issue adjusted invoice & credit memo.

Elisa (VP Finance): @Morgan reviewed. Approve a one-time $2,000 goodwill credit, note in ledger as customer retention credit. No SLA credit. Make sure sales documents the renewal condition.

Naomi (Acct): Will issue credit memo CM-2026-089 for $2,000 and send revised invoice. Adding note: customer error (client loop) + retention credit.

Bryan (Ops): For postmortem: I'll coordinate a short runbook update recommending rate-limiting patterns we can share with customers to avoid runaway short-lived sessions.

Sam (Sales): Thanks all — I'll follow up with BrightPath and share the renewal timeline.

Morgan (Finance): Closing loop: charge reconciled, $2,000 credit approved, no SLA credit. Marking this resolved unless anyone objects. :white_check_mark:
